question.text:
Find the truth set of $P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $\mathbb{R}{:}$

  • $P(x):$ $2x +1 \leq 7$

  • $Q(x):$ $x > 1$
question.explanation:
Since we have that

\[ P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x) \equiv \big(P(x) \land Q(x)\big) \lor \big(\neg P(x) \land \neg Q(x)\big), \]

the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} = (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q) \end{align*}

Now, we note the following:

  • To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} 2x +1 &\leq 7 \\[5pt] 2x &\leq 6 \\[5pt] x &\leq 3 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is $ T_P = (-\infty,3] $ and its complement is $ \overline{T}_P = (3,\infty). $

  • The truth set of $Q(x)$ is $ T_Q = (1,\infty) $ and its complement is $ \overline{T}_Q = (-\infty,1]. $

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_P \cap T_Q &= (-\infty,3] \cap (1,\infty) \\[5pt] &= (1,3] \\[10pt] \overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q &= (3,\infty) \cap (-\infty,1] \\[5pt] &= \emptyset \\[10pt] T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} &= (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q)\\[5pt] &= (1,3] \cup \emptyset \\[5pt] &= (1,3]. \end{align*}

question.text:
$\qquad$ If $x\in \mathbb{N},$ then $x$ is positive.

Which of the following is logically equivalent to the conditional predicate above?
question.explanation:
Let's denote by $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ the following predicates:

  • $P(x){:}$ $x\in \mathbb{N}.$

  • $Q(x){:}$ $x$ is positive.

Then, our initial sentence can be written as $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x),$ which is logically equivalent to

\[ \neg P(x) \lor Q(x). \]

The negation of $P(x)$ can be written as

  • $\neg P(x){:}$ $x\notin \mathbb{N}.$

Therefore, the given sentence is logically equivalent to the following:

$\qquad$ $x\notin \mathbb{N},$ or $x$ is positive.

question.text:
$\qquad$ If $x>2,$ then $x^3>3.$

Which of the following is logically equivalent to the conditional predicate above?
question.explanation:
Let's denote by $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ the following predicates:

  • $P(x){:}$ $x>2.$

  • $Q(x){:}$ $x^3>3.$

Then, our initial sentence can be written as $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x),$ which is logically equivalent to

\[ \neg P(x) \lor Q(x). \]

The negation of $P(x)$ can be written as

  • $\neg P(x){:}$ $x\leq 2.$

Therefore, the given sentence is logically equivalent to the following:

$\qquad$ $x\leq 2,$ or $x^3>3.$

example.title: Using Laws Involving Implications and Equivalences

question.text:
Consider the following predicates.

$\qquad$ $A(x):$ $x\in \mathbb {Z} \setminus \mathbb {N}_0.$ $\qquad$ $B(x):$ $x\in\mathbb {Z}^{-}.$

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate $A(x) \Leftrightarrow B(x)?$

  1. $x\in \mathbb {Z} \setminus \mathbb {N}_0$ if and only if $x\in\mathbb {Z}^{-}.$
  2. If $x\in \mathbb {Z}\setminus \mathbb {N}_0$ then $x\in \mathbb{Z}^{-},$ or if $x\in \mathbb{Z}^{-}$ then $x\in \mathbb {Z}\setminus \mathbb {N}_0.$
  3. $x\in \mathbb {Z} \setminus \mathbb {N}_0$ is equivalent to $x\in \mathbb{Z}^{-}.$
question.explanation:
A biconditional expression $P \Leftrightarrow Q \equiv (P \Rightarrow Q) \land (Q \Rightarrow P)$ can be read as shown below:

  • $P$ if and only if $Q$

  • $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

  • If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

So, $A \Leftrightarrow B$ translates into the following sentences:

  • $x\in \mathbb {Z} \setminus \mathbb {N}_0$ if and only if $x\in\mathbb {Z}^{-}.$

  • $x\in \mathbb {Z} \setminus \mathbb {N}_0$ is equivalent to $x\in \mathbb{Z}^{-}.$

  • If $x\in \mathbb {Z}\setminus \mathbb {N}_0$ then $x\in \mathbb{Z}^{-},$ and if $x\in \mathbb{Z}^{-}$ then $x\in \mathbb {Z}\setminus \mathbb {N}_0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
